q: What are the atomic number and valency (tetravalency) of carbon respectively?
e: Carbon has atomic number 6 (configuration 2, 4), giving it a valency of 4 (tetravalent).

q: The unique property of carbon atoms to link with other carbon atoms forming long chains, branches, or rings is called:
e: Catenation is carbon's self-linking property to form straight chains, branched chains, or closed rings.

q: Chemical bonds formed by the sharing of an electron pair between two atoms are known as:
e: Bonds formed by mutual sharing of valence electrons are called covalent bonds.

q: What is the general formula of alkanes? [JAC 2021]
e: Alkanes have general formula CnH2n+2, alkenes have CnH2n, and alkynes have CnH2n-2.

q: What is the general formula of alkenes? [JAC 2020]
e: Alkenes contain at least one carbon-carbon double bond and follow the general formula CnH2n.

q: What is the general formula of alkynes?
e: Alkynes contain a triple bond between carbons and have the general formula CnH2n-2.

q: Which of the following is an unsaturated hydrocarbon? [JAC 2024]
e: C2H2 (ethyne) contains a triple bond making it unsaturated, whereas CH4, C2H6, and C4H10 are saturated alkanes.

q: How many covalent bonds are present in one molecule of methane (CH4)?
e: Methane has 4 single C—H covalent bonds.

q: In which of the following compounds is —OH the functional group? [JAC 2025]
e: The —OH (alcohol) functional group uses the suffix "-ol", as in butanol.

q: What is the functional group present in HCHO? [JAC 2024]
e: The —CHO group represents the aldehyde functional group.

q: What is the IUPAC name of the compound CH3—CH2—CHO? [JAC 2025, 2026]
e: The chain has 3 carbons (prop-) and an aldehyde group —CHO (-al), giving the name propanal.

q: What is the formula of the carboxylic acid functional group?
e: The carboxylic acid functional group is —COOH.

q: What is the minimum number of carbon atoms in the simplest ketone (propanone)?
e: A carbonyl group in a ketone must be flanked by two carbons, so the simplest ketone is propanone (CH3COCH3) with 3 carbons.

q: Vinegar is a 5–8% aqueous solution of which organic acid?
e: A 5–8% solution of ethanoic (acetic) acid in water is called vinegar and is widely used as a preservative in pickles.

q: Pure ethanoic acid melts at 290 K and often freezes during winter in cold climates, hence it is known as:
e: Pure ethanoic acid freezes into glacier-like crystals in winter (m.p. 290 K), earning the name glacial acetic acid.

q: Buckminsterfullerene (C-60), shaped like a football, is an allotrope of:
e: Fullerenes (such as C-60 Buckminsterfullerene) are allotropes of carbon alongside diamond and graphite.

q: What is the molecular formula of benzene and how many C=C double bonds are in its ring?
e: Benzene (C6H6) is a hexagonal ring with 3 alternating carbon-carbon double bonds.

q: Successive members of a homologous series differ in molecular formula and molecular mass by:
e: Adjacent members of any homologous series differ by one —CH2 unit and 14 atomic mass units (u).

q: Which of the following is NOT observed in a homologous series? [JAC 2025]
e: Members of a homologous series share the same functional group and hence have similar chemical properties, not changing chemical properties.

q: Saturated hydrocarbons burn in sufficient oxygen with what kind of flame?
e: Saturated hydrocarbons normally burn with a clean blue flame, whereas unsaturated hydrocarbons give a yellow sooty flame.

q: If the bottom of a cooking vessel turns black on a gas stove, it means:
o: Air holes are blocked and the fuel is burning incompletely
e: Blocked air inlets restrict oxygen supply, causing incomplete combustion and deposition of unburnt carbon soot.

q: Which catalyst is used in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils to form saturated fats (vanaspati ghee)?
e: Hydrogenation (addition of H2 across double bonds) uses nickel or palladium catalysts.

q: Which gas is evolved when ethanol reacts with sodium metal?
e: Sodium reacts with ethanol producing sodium ethoxide and liberating hydrogen gas.

q: Heating ethanol at 443 K with excess concentrated sulphuric acid gives:
e: Concentrated H2SO4 acts as a dehydrating agent, removing water from ethanol to form unsaturated ethene.

q: The conversion of ethanol to ethanoic acid is an example of which reaction? [JAC 2020]
e: Ethanol gains oxygen using oxidising agents like alkaline KMnO4 or acidified K2Cr2O7 to form ethanoic acid, so it is oxidation.

q: The reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol in presence of acid catalyst to form a sweet-smelling compound is called:
e: Acid and alcohol react to form sweet-smelling esters and water in an esterification reaction.

q: What are the two distinct ends of a soap molecule?
o: One ionic hydrophilic head and one long hydrocarbon hydrophobic tail
e: Soap molecules have a water-attracting ionic end (—COO⁻Na⁺) and an oil-attracting hydrocarbon tail.

q: The spherical clusters formed by soap molecules trapping oily dirt inside water are called:
e: In a micelle, hydrophobic tails point inward toward oily dirt while ionic heads face outward into water, emulsifying dirt.

q: Why are detergents effective even in hard water whereas ordinary soap forms scum?
o: Charged ends of detergents do not form insoluble precipitates (scum) with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions in hard water
e: Soap reacts with Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ to form insoluble scum, whereas detergents remain soluble and lather well in hard water.

q: Ethane, with the molecular formula C2H6, has how many covalent bonds? [NCERT]
e: Ethane has 1 C—C bond and 6 C—H bonds, totalling 7 covalent bonds.

q: Butanone is a four-carbon compound with which functional group? [NCERT]
e: The suffix "-one" identifies the ketone functional group (CH3COCH2CH3).

q: Which reagent helps easily distinguish between ethanol and ethanoic acid in a laboratory test?
e: Ethanoic acid reacts briskly with NaHCO3 liberating CO2 gas (turning lime water milky), whereas ethanol gives no reaction.

q: What are the products formed when ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate (Na2CO3)?
e: Ethanoic acid reacts with carbonates to produce sodium ethanoate, water, and carbon dioxide.

q: In saponification, an ester is heated with what reagent to regenerate alcohol and form soap?
e: Heating an ester with NaOH breaks it back into alcohol and sodium salt of the carboxylic acid (soap).

q: Which chemical test distinguishes unsaturated hydrocarbons (like cooking oil) from saturated ones (like butter)?
e: Unsaturated compounds undergo addition with bromine water and decolourise its reddish-brown colour, while saturated compounds do not.

q: What type of covalent bond exists between the two nitrogen atoms in an N2 molecule?
e: Each nitrogen atom (2,5) shares 3 electrons with the other to complete its octet, forming a triple bond (N≡N).

q: How many pairs of electrons are shared between two oxygen atoms to form an O2 molecule?
e: Oxygen atoms (2,6) share 2 pairs of electrons to form a double covalent bond (O=O).

q: Mixing poisonous methanol and dye into industrial ethanol to make it unfit for drinking produces:
e: Denatured alcohol is ethanol rendered poisonous and blue-dyed with methanol/dyes to prevent unlawful consumption.

q: How many structural isomers are possible for butane (C4H10)?
e: Butane (C4H10) exhibits 2 structural isomers: n-butane and 2-methylpropane (iso-butane).

q: How many structural isomers can you draw for pentane (C5H12)? [NCERT]
e: Pentane has exactly 3 structural isomers: n-pentane, 2-methylbutane, and 2,2-dimethylpropane.

q: Why can ingesting even a small quantity of methanol prove fatal or cause blindness?
o: Liver oxidises methanol to methanal, which coagulates protoplasm and damages the optic nerve
e: Methanol is oxidised in the liver to methanal, rapidly reacting with cell components, coagulating protoplasm, and harming the optic nerve.

q: Which carbon compound is a good solvent used in tincture of iodine, cough syrups, and many tonics?
e: Ethanol is an important solvent used in tincture iodine, cough syrups, and medicinal tonics.

q: The reaction CH4 + Cl2 → CH3Cl + HCl in the presence of sunlight is known as:
e: In sunlight, chlorine atoms replace hydrogen atoms one by one in saturated methane—a substitution reaction.

q: What is the molecular formula of cyclopentane?
e: Cycloalkanes have the general formula CnH2n with all single bonds, so cyclopentane is C5H10.

q: Diamond and graphite differ widely in physical properties yet both burn completely to yield only CO2 gas. Why?
o: Both are allotropes of the same element carbon with identical chemical properties but different bonding structures
e: Both consist solely of carbon atoms arranged differently (3D tetrahedral in diamond vs hexagonal sheets in graphite), giving identical chemistry.

q: In diamond's rigid three-dimensional structure, each carbon atom is bonded to how many other carbon atoms?
e: Each carbon atom in diamond bonds covalently to 4 neighbouring carbons in a rigid 3D tetrahedral network.

q: In graphite, each carbon atom is bonded to how many other carbon atoms in the same hexagonal layer?
e: Each carbon in graphite bonds to 3 others in flat hexagonal sheets, leaving one free electron per carbon for conduction.

q: What is the shape of the S8 molecule of sulphur?
e: Eight sulphur atoms link together covalently in a puckered crown-shaped ring (S8).

q: Which simplest alkane is the major constituent of CNG and biogas? [JAC 2022]
e: Methane (CH4) is the primary fuel component of compressed natural gas (CNG) and biogas.

q: Identify the heteroatoms present in chloropropane and bromobutane respectively:
e: Cl and Br replace hydrogen in these haloalkanes and act as heteroatoms.

q: In the conversion of ethanol to ethanoic acid, alkaline KMnO4 or acidified K2Cr2O7 acts as:
e: Substances like alkaline KMnO4 and acidified K2Cr2O7 supply oxygen to convert alcohols to acids, acting as oxidising agents.

q: Why are vegetable oils (containing unsaturated fatty acids) recommended for cooking over saturated animal fats?
o: Animal fats contain saturated fatty acids harmful to health, whereas vegetable oils have unsaturated chains
e: Saturated fatty acids in animal fats are considered harmful for health, so oils with unsaturated carbon chains are preferred.

q: When alkaline KMnO4 is added drop by drop to warm ethanol, why does the pink colour initially disappear?
o: KMnO4 is consumed as it oxidises ethanol to ethanoic acid
e: Initially, all KMnO4 added is consumed in oxidising ethanol, causing its purple/pink colour to disappear until oxidation finishes.

q: Why do carbon (covalent) compounds generally have low melting and boiling points compared to ionic compounds?
o: The intermolecular forces of attraction between covalent molecules are relatively weak
e: Although bonds within a covalent molecule are strong, the forces between separate molecules are weak, giving low m.p. and b.p.

q: Burning coal and petroleum produces acid-rain pollutants (oxides) due to small amounts of which two elements present in them?
e: Traces of nitrogen and sulphur in fossil fuels combust to form oxides of nitrogen and sulphur, major pollutants.

q: Which alcohol is produced by fermenting molasses from sugarcane juice and is used as a clean fuel additive in petrol?
e: Fermentation of sugarcane molasses produces ethanol, which is blended into petrol as a cleaner-burning fuel additive.

q: An unsaturated hydrocarbon MUST contain at least one:
o: C=C double bond or C≡C triple bond
e: Hydrocarbons having double (C=C) or triple (C≡C) bonds between carbon atoms are unsaturated.

q: While forming a micelle in water, which part of soap aligns towards oil/dirt and which towards water?
o: Ionic end to oil, tail to water
Hydrocarbon tail dissolves in oil/dirt, while ionic head faces outward toward water
e: The non-polar hydrocarbon tail embeds into oily dirt while the polar ionic end stays oriented toward water.

q: Which homologous series starts with a 2-carbon compound (n = 2) rather than a 1-carbon compound?
e: Forming a carbon-carbon double or triple bond requires at least two carbon atoms, so alkenes and alkynes start at C2.

q: Which compound is formed at the final step of complete chlorination of methane in sunlight?
e: Sequential substitution replaces all four hydrogens with chlorine atoms, ending with carbon tetrachloride (CCl4).

q: What is the molecular formula of propyne and what bond does it contain?
e: Putting n=3 in CnH2n-2 gives C3H4 (CH3—C≡CH), featuring a carbon-carbon triple bond.

q: Select the correct pair of IUPAC names for CH3—CO—CH2—CH3 and CH3—CH2—CH2—CHO respectively:
e: Both have 4 carbons: the first has an internal ketone (>C=O) making it butanone; the second has a terminal —CHO making it butanal.

q: Identify the correct match for Acetylene, Formic acid, and Propanol formulas: [JAC 2020]
e: Acetylene is H—C≡C—H, formic acid is HCOOH, and 1-propanol is CH3CH2CH2OH.

q: Which two among methanol (CH3OH), butanol (C4H9OH), and chloropentane (C5H11Cl) belong to the SAME homologous series? [JAC 2024]
e: Methanol and butanol both share the —OH functional group and CnH2n+1OH formula, belonging to the alcohol homologous series.

q: Which pair of functional isomers shares the exact same molecular formula C3H6O?
e: Propanal and propanone both have formula C3H6O while differing in functional group (aldehyde vs ketone).

q: What are the molecular formulas of Hexene and Benzene respectively? [JAC 2020, 2021]
e: Hexene follows CnH2n giving C6H12, whereas benzene has formula C6H6.

q: Which of the following hydrocarbons undergo addition reactions: C2H6, C3H8, C3H6, C2H2, CH4? [NCERT]
e: Only unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkene C3H6 and alkyne C2H2) undergo addition reactions; alkanes undergo substitution.

q: How are esterification (acid + alcohol) and alkaline hydrolysis of ester (saponification) related?
o: Esterification forms an ester from acid and alcohol, whereas saponification splits the ester back into alcohol and salt of acid
e: Esterification synthesises an ester; saponification hydrolyses the ester back to the alcohol and carboxylic acid salt.

q: How many total single covalent bonds exist in one molecule of butane (C4H10)?
e: Butane has 3 C—C single bonds and 10 C—H single bonds, giving 13 covalent bonds in total.

q: What is the fourth member of the alkane homologous series and its molecular formula?
e: The 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th alkanes are methane (CH4), ethane (C2H6), propane (C3H8), and butane (C4H10).

q: As molecular mass increases along a homologous series, how do melting and boiling points change?
o: Increase gradually due to stronger intermolecular attractions
e: Increased molecular size and mass strengthen intermolecular forces, causing melting and boiling points to increase systematically.

q: Identify the 2nd and 3rd members of the alcohol homologous series and the mass difference between them:
e: Ethanol (C2H5OH, 46 u) and propanol (C3H7OH, 60 u) are the 2nd and 3rd members, differing by 14 u.

q: An organic compound X (formula C2H4O2) reacts with Na to give H2 and with NaHCO3 to give brisk CO2 effervescence. Identify X:
e: C2H4O2 corresponds to ethanoic acid (CH3COOH), which liberates H2 with Na and CO2 with NaHCO3.

q: Ethanol (m.p. 156 K, b.p. 351 K) is liquid at room temperature whereas methane (b.p. 111 K) is a gas. What is the boiling point of pure ethanoic acid?
e: Per NCERT Table 4.1, ethanoic acid melts at 290 K and boils at 391 K, while ethanol boils at 351 K.

q: Hydrogen bromide (HBr) adds across the double bond of ethene (C2H4) to produce:
e: Addition of HBr across ethene's double bond forms bromoethane.

q: Complete oxidation of propan-1-ol (CH3CH2CH2OH) using alkaline KMnO4 yields:
e: A 3-carbon primary alcohol oxidises to the corresponding 3-carbon carboxylic acid: propanoic acid.

q: Hard water prevents soap from lathering properly due to dissolved salts of which ions?
e: Calcium and magnesium ions in hard water precipitate soap molecules as insoluble calcium/magnesium salts (scum).

q: Compare hydrocarbons with molecular formulas C4H8 and C4H6. They represent respectively:
e: C4H8 fits CnH2n (butene) and C4H6 fits CnH2n-2 (butyne).

q: The "lead" in a common writing pencil contains no lead metal at all, but is made of:
e: Graphite's hexagonal layers slide smoothly over each other, leaving dark marks on paper; hence it is used in pencils.

q: What is the nature of an aqueous solution of sodium ethanoate (CH3COONa)?
o: Basic (pH > 7), as it is a salt of weak acid and strong base
e: Being formed from weak ethanoic acid and strong NaOH, sodium ethanoate produces a mildly basic solution.

q: In the electron dot structure of CO2, how many shared pairs exist between carbon and EACH oxygen atom?
e: Carbon shares 2 electron pairs with each oxygen atom, forming two double bonds: O=C=O.

q: In the esterification reaction CH3COOH + C2H5OH ⇌ CH3COOC2H5 + H2O, what role does conc. H2SO4 play?
o: Catalyst and dehydrating agent (removes water to favour ester formation)
e: Conc. H2SO4 catalyses the reaction and absorbs formed water to shift equilibrium towards the ester.

q: How are atoms bonded around carbon in chloromethane (CH3Cl)?
o: 3 H atoms and 1 Cl atom via single covalent bonds
e: In CH3Cl, carbon forms three single bonds with H and one single bond with Cl.

q: Why is a mixture of oxygen and ethyne (rather than air) burnt for welding metals?
o: Ethyne burns incompletely in air with soot, whereas pure oxygen gives complete combustion and very high temperature
e: In air, ethyne burns incompletely with soot and lower heat; burning in pure oxygen causes complete combustion with an extremely hot flame for welding.

q: Why are unsaturated vegetable oils typically liquid at room temperature whereas hydrogenated fats (vanaspati ghee) are semi-solid?
o: Double bonds create kinks preventing tight packing, while saturated chains pack closely into solids
e: Hydrogenation removes double bonds, allowing saturated chains to pack neatly and raise the melting point.

q: Among C—C, C=C, and C≡C bonds, which bond is the shortest and strongest?
e: Sharing three electron pairs pulls the two carbon nuclei closest together, making the C≡C triple bond shortest and strongest.

q: Methanoic acid and ethanoic acid are the first two members of which homologous series?
e: Both possess the —COOH group and differ by —CH2, making them consecutive carboxylic acids.

q: What salt is produced when ethanoic acid reacts with sodium hydroxide solution?
e: Neutralisation of ethanoic acid with NaOH gives sodium ethanoate and water.

q: What are the name and molecular formula of the THIRD member of the alkene series?
e: Since ethene (C2H4) is 1st and propene (C3H6) is 2nd, the 3rd alkene is butene (C4H8).

q: Which two key factors enable carbon to form millions of diverse organic compounds?
e: Carbon's strong catenation ability and tetravalency allow it to bond with carbon and heteroatoms to form millions of compounds.

q: Compound A (C2H6O) oxidises with alkaline KMnO4 to B. Heating A and B with conc. H2SO4 produces sweet-smelling C. Identify A, B, C:
e: A is ethanol, which oxidises to ethanoic acid (B); esterification of A and B gives ethyl ethanoate (C).

q: How can you chemically distinguish between liquid cooking oil and melted butter/vanaspati ghee?
o: Adding bromine water: the unsaturated vegetable oil decolourises it, whereas saturated fat does not
e: Unsaturated vegetable oil decolourises bromine water via addition reaction, unlike saturated fats.

q: Equal amounts of soap and detergent are shaken separately in two test tubes containing hard water. Which tube produces greater foam height?
o: More in detergent tube (since detergents do not form scum in hard water)
e: Detergent produces abundant lather in hard water without wasting itself forming insoluble scum.

q: An organic compound turns blue litmus red and is a weak electrolyte in water. Which compound could it be?
e: Ethanoic acid ionises weakly in water to produce H⁺ ions, turning blue litmus red.

q: If a kitchen LPG stove burns with a yellow sooty flame blackening utensils, what corrective step fixes it?
o: Clean the clogged air holes of the burner to allow sufficient air/oxygen for complete combustion
e: Unclogging burner air holes restores proper oxygen flow for clean, complete combustion with a blue flame.

q: A student reacts ethanoic acid with sodium carbonate and passes the evolved gas into lime water. What is observed?
o: Lime water turns milky, confirming CO2 gas
e: Evolved CO2 reacts with lime water to turn it milky due to CaCO3 formation.

q: How do soap micelles clean oily dirt from clothes when rinsed with water?
o: Oily dirt trapped inside micelle centres stays suspended as an emulsion/colloid in water and rinses away
e: Negatively charged outer shells of micelles repel each other so micelles stay suspended in water and rinse away easily.

q: Compounds X (C3H8O), Y (C4H10O), and Z (C5H12O) belong to the same alcohol homologous series. Which statement is true?
o: All three share —OH group and similar chemical properties, while boiling point increases X < Y < Z
e: Chemical properties stay similar across the series while boiling points increase from X to Z with molecular mass.

q: Which comparison between ethanol and ethanoic acid is INCORRECT?
o: Both are liquids at room temp
Ethanol is neutral whereas ethanoic acid turns blue litmus red
Both react with NaHCO3 to liberate CO2
Ethanol boils at 351 K and ethanoic acid at 391 K
e: Only ethanoic acid reacts with NaHCO3 to evolve CO2; ethanol does not.

q: Which compounds among C2H6, C3H6, C4H6, and C6H6 will decolourise bromine water?
e: Alkenes (C3H6) and alkynes (C4H6) readily undergo addition to decolourise bromine water (aromatic benzene resists ordinary addition).

q: When does a burning substance produce a visible flame, and why does charcoal glow red without a flame?
o: A flame is produced only when gaseous substances burn; charcoal lacks volatile gases once lit so it glows without a flame
e: Flames appear only when gaseous/vaporised matter burns; non-volatile carbon in charcoal simply glows red without a flame.

q: Which reagent dehydrates propan-1-ol (CH3CH2CH2OH) on heating to yield propene (CH3CH=CH2)?
e: Excess concentrated H2SO4 dehydrates alcohols upon heating to produce alkenes.

q: Identify the 2-carbon compound with formula C2H4O and suffix "-al":
e: Two carbons ("eth-") plus aldehyde suffix ("-al") gives ethanal (CH3CHO).

q: Coal and petroleum were formed over millions of years from:
o: Biomass of ancient trees/ferns (coal) and marine organisms (petroleum) compressed under high pressure and heat
e: Coal formed from buried land plants and petroleum/natural gas from buried marine organisms under high heat and pressure.

q: Dropping a small piece of sodium into which liquid produces sodium ethoxide and H2 gas?
e: Sodium reacts smoothly with ethanol to form sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas.

q: How many single bonds and double bonds are present in one molecule of benzene (C6H6)?
o: 9 single (3 C—C + 6 C—H) and 3 double (C=C) bonds
e: Benzene has 3 alternating C=C double bonds, 3 C—C single bonds, and 6 C—H single bonds, giving 9 single and 3 double bonds.

q: How many total covalent bonds (shared electron pairs) are in one molecule of propanone (CH3COCH3)?
e: Propanone contains 2 C—C single bonds, 6 C—H single bonds, and 1 C=O double bond (2 pairs), totalling 10 shared electron pairs.

q: Hydrocarbon A (C2H4) decolourises bromine water and gives B (C2H6) upon catalytic hydrogenation. What does B form with Cl2 in sunlight?
e: A is ethene and B is saturated ethane; in sunlight ethane undergoes substitution with chlorine to form chloroethane.

q: Between 1 mole of methane (CH4) and 1 mole of ethyne (C2H2), which requires MORE moles of O2 for complete combustion?
e: CH4 needs 2 moles O2 per mole, whereas C2H2 needs 2.5 moles O2 per mole for complete combustion.

q: Heating sodium ethanoate (CH3COONa) with soda-lime (NaOH + CaO) produces which alkane gas?
e: Decarboxylation of sodium ethanoate with soda-lime removes CO2 as Na2CO3, forming methane gas (CH4).

q: Compounds with formula C3H6O2 can exist as propanoic acid (CH3CH2COOH) or as:
o: Ester (such as methyl ethanoate CH3COOCH3 or ethyl methanoate)
e: Carboxylic acids and esters share the general formula CnH2nO2 and behave as functional isomers.

q: Why does micelle formation NOT take place when soap is added to ethanol instead of water?
o: The hydrocarbon tail of soap is soluble in ethanol, so molecules disperse individually without clustering into micelles
e: Since soap's hydrocarbon chain dissolves freely in organic ethanol, there is no hydrophobic push to form micelles.

q: How many open-chain structural isomers exist for the alkene formula C4H8?
e: Open-chain C4H8 has 3 structural isomers: but-1-ene, but-2-ene, and 2-methylpropene.

q: How many moles of H2 gas are needed to fully saturate 1 mole each of ethene (C2H4), ethyne (C2H2), and ethane (C2H6)?
e: Ethene needs 1 mole H2, ethyne needs 2 moles H2 to convert C≡C to single bond, and saturated ethane needs 0.

q: Why does 0.1 M ethanoic acid have a much higher pH (~2.9) than 0.1 M HCl (pH 1)?
o: Ethanoic acid is a weak acid that ionises only partially (~1%) giving fewer free H⁺ ions than fully ionised HCl
e: Partial ionisation of weak ethanoic acid yields far fewer H⁺ ions than complete dissociation of strong HCl.

q: Which hydrocarbon has the highest mass percentage of carbon (~92.3%), causing maximum soot when burnt in air?
e: In ethyne (C2H2), 24 out of 26 atomic mass units is carbon (92.3%), giving the highest soot formation in air.

q: What is the general formula of a monovalent alkyl group (like methyl, ethyl)?
e: Removing one H atom from an alkane (CnH2n+2) produces the corresponding alkyl radical CnH2n+1—.

q: In which pair do BOTH compounds end with the IUPAC suffix "-one"?
e: Both propanone and pentan-3-one contain the ketone group (>C=O) and take the "-one" suffix.

q: Why does the solubility of alcohols in water decrease as the carbon chain grows longer from methanol to hexanol?
o: The non-polar hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail becomes larger and dominates over the polar —OH head
e: The hydrophilic —OH head gets outweighed by the growing hydrophobic alkyl tail as chain length increases.

q: When equal pieces of sodium are dropped into pure water and pure ethanol separately, where is H2 evolution much more vigorous?
o: In pure water, because water reacts much more vigorously with sodium than ethanol
e: Sodium reacts violently with water (catching fire) whereas it sinks and reacts gently in ethanol.

q: In one molecule of propene (CH3—CH=CH2), how many C—C single bonds, C=C double bonds, and C—H single bonds exist?
o: 1 C—C single, 1 C=C double bond, and 6 C—H single bonds
e: Propene (CH3—CH=CH2) features 1 C—C single bond, 1 C=C double bond, and 6 C—H single bonds.

q: When methanoic acid (HCOOH) reacts with ethanol (C2H5OH) in presence of conc. H2SO4, what is the IUPAC name of the sweet-smelling ester formed?
e: The alkyl part comes from ethanol (ethyl) and the acid part from methanoic acid (methanoate), giving ethyl methanoate.

q: The football-like Buckminsterfullerene (C60) cage consists of interlocking rings of:
e: Just like a classic soccer ball, C60 consists of 20 hexagonal and 12 pentagonal carbon rings.

q: One volume of gaseous hydrocarbon X consumes 3 volumes of O2 upon complete combustion to yield 2 volumes of CO2 and steam. Identify X:
e: C2H4 + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 2H2O matches the exact 1 : 3 : 2 volume ratio.

q: Identify the gases evolved when ethanoic acid reacts with (i) Sodium metal and (ii) Sodium bicarbonate respectively:
e: Sodium metal displaces H2 gas from ethanoic acid, whereas NaHCO3 evolves CO2 gas.

q: What type of structural difference exists between but-1-ene and but-2-ene?
o: Difference in the position of the C=C double bond
e: Both have 4 carbons and one double bond, differing solely in whether the double bond is at C1 or C2.

q: Arrange Benzene (C6H6), Cyclohexane (C6H12), and Hexane (C6H14) in increasing order of hydrogen atoms per molecule:
o: Benzene (6 H) < Cyclohexane (12 H) < Hexane (14 H)
e: For 6 carbons: Benzene has 6 H atoms, Cyclohexane has 12 H atoms, and Hexane has 14 H atoms.

q: Which of the following pairs contains ONLY C, H, and a halogen heteroatom (no oxygen)?
e: Bromoethane and chloropentane are haloalkanes without oxygen, whereas aldehydes and alcohols contain oxygen.

q: Neutralising ethanoic acid completely with aqueous NaOH yields which salt?
e: Ethanoic acid + NaOH produces sodium ethanoate (CH3COONa) + water, whereas Na + ethanol produces sodium ethoxide.

q: What happens if a few drops of dilute HCl are added to an aqueous soap solution?
o: Insoluble free fatty acid (stearic acid) precipitates out and soap stops lathering
e: Strong HCl displaces the weak long-chain fatty acid, precipitating insoluble stearic acid and stopping lather.

q: Besides carbon, which common non-metal prominently exhibits allotropy (white, red, black forms)?
e: Phosphorus (white, red, black) and sulphur (rhombic, monoclinic) prominently display allotropy like carbon.

q: Which cyclic SATURATED hydrocarbon shares the same molecular formula C6H12 as hexene (an alkene)?
e: Cyclohexane is a 6-membered saturated ring (C6H12) with all C—C single bonds, isomeric with hexene.

q: Carbon compounds like CO2, CO, और CaCO3 contain carbon, yet why are they studied under INORGANIC rather than organic chemistry?
o: Obeying historical/structural convention, oxides, carbonates, and carbides lack hydrocarbon frameworks and belong to inorganic chemistry
e: As noted in NCERT, oxides of carbon, carbonates, and hydrogen carbonates are classified as inorganic compounds.

q: Why is a few drops of concentrated H2SO4 necessary during esterification in a school lab?
o: Without an acid catalyst, esterification is extremely slow and reversible back towards reactants
e: Esterification is very slow and reversible; conc. H2SO4 speeds it up as a catalyst and absorbs water.

q: Which zone of a candle flame represents complete combustion and is the hottest region?
e: The outermost non-luminous blue zone has abundant oxygen access for complete combustion, making it the hottest part.
